state: WITNESS IMPLEMENTED — all 25 sites target-bounded; measurement complete; independent review pending

fact.statement: The twenty-five element-7 sites all read one member of a provider cipher hardware method table through the `hw` sub-struct of their context. Every such table is a file-scope `static` literal whose members are compile-time function pointers; the context's `hw` pointer is stored only by a closed set of constructors from that closed table set. Therefore each site's target set is finite and fully enumerable.

writer_closure.method_fields: no member of any hw table is assigned at run time: a source scan of src/provider/cipher.rs and src/provider/cipher_gcm.rs finds zero `(*...).<member> =` stores; every member value comes from a `static` initialiser
writer_closure.context_pointer: the `hw` pointer itself has one production writer per context type (table below); each writer's value is a named static table, or a selector that returns one
writer_closure.whole_struct_copies: the row `*_dupctx` bodies copy the whole context block (CRYPTO_memdup / copy_nonoverlapping). A copy preserves the `hw` pointer value and introduces no new target; it is listed per context type rather than treated as a writer of a new value

fact.caveat: This class is NOT a public external ABI contract. It is an internal, closed static-table dispatch whose target set is finite and enumerated. It is admitted into ABI_CONTRACT_CLASSES exactly as ABI_CONTRACT_SLH_METHOD_TABLE is, and its resolution_kind records 'target-bounded by a closed file-scope static set', not 'contract-bounded (target set unbounded)'. Element 7 remains FAIL at this candidate (31 reachable target-bounded sites), so no element-7 PASS is claimed from this classification.
